genericProblem: A UI design can declare an exported shared-foundation primitive solely because it exists, causing a later declaration-to-import control to revive a primitive already retained as dormant and unrelated to the user's task.
rootCauseClass: Export existence was treated as sufficient reuse evidence; the design admission lacked a required readback of production consumers and documented dormant or retirement disposition.
counterexamples: A new, business-required foundation primitive can legitimately have zero current production consumers when the declared screen is explicitly designed as its first and uniquely owned consumer.
An exported primitive with active consumers is not rejected merely because it is implemented in foundation rather than locally.

The overview page's refresh and retry are valid user actions; only the dormant RefreshSignal dependency is removed, while the generated RTK query refetch behavior remains its source-backed implementation path.

findings.evidence: IA02-PLATFORM-WORKSPACE-OVERVIEW declared createRefreshSignal/useRefreshVersion. useRefreshVersion has no production consumer; P5 records RefreshSignal publish sites without a production subscriber and RTK tags as the refresh authority; the all-v2 counterpart uses generated query refetch().
The cross-IA declaration scan finds createRefreshSignal/useRefreshVersion only in IA02-PLATFORM-WORKSPACE-OVERVIEW; no other IA-01/IA-02 screen declares either dormant refresh primitive.
